question:
“_______ grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid, e.g., Marchantia. The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures.”

The above statement signifies which of the following Bryophyta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Liverworts.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Liverworts, like the species seen over, represent a branch of non-vascular shops, the utmost of which are terrestrial.
 
• The name “ liverworts ” is deduced from the belief in ancient times that the conditions of the liver could be cured with these shops.
 
• Liverworts are part of the area Plantae, in the division Marchantiophyta.
 
• While the shops are small, and frequently overlooked, liverworts can be set up encyclopedically, wherever shops can grow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Selaginella:**

 
 
• Selaginella is a pteridophyte.
 
• It is also called spikemoss or club moss.
 
• It is the largest and the only living genus of the family Selaginellaceae.
 
 
 
• **Salvinia:**
 
 
• Belonging to the family Salviniaceae, Salvinia is its genus.
 
• Generally, it's addressed as water moss. These species are related to the other water ferns similar to the mosquito fern, Azolla. Salvinia is heterosporous synthesizing spores of varying sizes.
 
 
 
• **Sphagnum:**
 
 
• Sphagnum is a genus of moss that's also generally known as peat moss, sphagnum moss, and bog moss.
 
• They're of ecological significance as they form peat that serves as carbon sinks in the ecosystem.
 
• It grows in wet and boggy areas and requires acidic soil.
